correctness.rationale: For \(a,b\ge2\), each maximal-chain facet has primitive inward normal \(-e_i-e_j-e_k\). For a distinguished coordinate ray, an alternate outer-tier coordinate forces other entries to vanish, except when \(c=1\) and the distinguished coordinate is the middle one, permitting a \(\{0,1\}\)-subset wholly inside one outer tier. Every coordinate belongs to another maximal-chain facet, so no maximal-chain ray can distinguish a root. These integer inequalities prove the infinite root enumeration, including the boundary cases. The Demazure-derivation brackets lower subset size by one, giving the vector-group semidirect product and a lower-central-series class exactly \(\max(a,b)+1\); when \(c\ge2\) all root brackets vanish. The included checker confirms \(30{,}861\) bounded exact cases only; no finite-to-infinite inference is used.

value.rationale: The sharp jump when the middle antichain changes size 1 to 2 turns an arbitrarily high-class, exponentially large unipotent radical into an abelian radical. Classifying complete connected automorphism groups, not only numerical invariants, for a classical natural infinite poset-polytope family supplies structural symmetry information that is potentially useful for studying toric degeneration symmetries and comparison between order and chain toric models.
